Let
\[
u=x(1+x)^{-1},\qquad Y=y-u,\qquad Z=z-u,
\]
where
\[
(1+x)^{-1}=\sum_{i=0}^{5m}(-x)^i
\]
is well-defined since \(x^{5m+1}=0\).

In these generators the defining relations become
\[
u^{5m+1}=0,\qquad Yu=\zeta uY,\qquad Zu=\zeta^{-1}uZ,\qquad ZY=\zeta YZ.
\]
Thus \(R_m\) has PBW basis
\[
u^aY^bZ^c,\qquad 0\le a\le 5m,\quad b,c\ge 0.
\]

For a basis monomial \(M=u^aY^bZ^c\), centrality gives:
\[
YM=\zeta^a u^aY^{b+1}Z^c,\qquad MY=\zeta^c u^aY^{b+1}Z^c,
\]
so \(a\equiv c\pmod 5\). Similarly,
\[
ZM=\zeta^{b-a}u^aY^bZ^{c+1},\qquad MZ=u^aY^bZ^{c+1},
\]
so \(a\equiv b\pmod 5\). Finally, commuting with \(u\) gives \(b\equiv c\pmod 5\), with the top nilpotent case \(a=5m\) already compatible. Hence the central monomials are exactly
\[
u^aY^bZ^c\quad\text{with}\quad a\equiv b\equiv c\pmod 5.
\]

Equivalently, the center is generated by
\[
u^5,\qquad Y^5,\qquad Z^5,\qquad uYZ.
\]

Therefore, in the original generators,
\[
\boxed{
Z(R_m)=
k\!\left[
\left(\frac{x}{1+x}\right)^5,\,
\left(y-\frac{x}{1+x}\right)^5,\,
\left(z-\frac{x}{1+x}\right)^5,\,
\frac{x}{1+x}\left(y-\frac{x}{1+x}\right)\left(z-\frac{x}{1+x}\right)
\right].
}
\]
Here \(\frac{x}{1+x}\) means \(x(1+x)^{-1}\) inside \(R_m\).
